questions.question: Who led the Bharat Jodo Yatra 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rahul Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Bharat Jodo Yatra:**

__
 
• It is **a political campaign organized by the Indian National Congress (INC)** to unite the people of India and promote national integration.
 
• Senior Congress leader **Rahul Gandhi initiated the movement** by motivating the party cadre and the public to embark on a **4,080 km journey** from **Kanyakumari(Tamil Nadu) to** the union territory of **Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• This journey **took almost 150 days to complete.**
 
• The march started from Kanyakumari on 7 September and ended on 30 January 2023.
 
 
• Rahul Gandhi unfurled the national tricolour at Lal Chowk in Srinagar bringing the padayatra to an end
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rahul Gandhi** is an Indian politician and **Member of Parliament** from INC representing **Wayanad, Kerala** in **Lok Sabha**.

 
 
• He previously represented the constituency of Amethi, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• He is the **chairperson** of the **Indian Youth Congress**, the **National Students Union of India** and a trustee of the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation and Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust.
 
• He was also the **president of INC from December 2017 to July 2019.**
 
 
 
• Sonia Gandhi is a former President of the Congress Party who served as its leader for over two decades, but she stepped down from the position in 2017 and is currently the Chairperson of the Congress Parliamentary Party.
 
 
• She is the** longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• She has been a **Member of Parliament in Lok Sabha from Rae Bareli constituency since 2004.**
 
 
 
• **Priyanka Gandhi** is a popular politician and the **general secretary of the All India Congress Committee in charge of Uttar Pradesh.**
 
 
• She is known for her charismatic personality and strong communication skills. She is the sister of Rahul Gandhi.

questions.question: Who among the following is the composer of Prayag Prashasti or the Allahabad Pillar in praise of Gupta ruler Samudra Gupta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Harishena.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harishena** was a **4th-century Sanskrit poet.** 
 
• He was a **court poet** and minister in the Gupta emperor **Samudragupta.**
 
• He is the **composer of Prayag Prashasti or the Allahabad Pillar** in praise of Gupta ruler Samudragupta.
 
• He was also the author of several other inscriptions and** **literary works, including the Junagadh rock inscription of Skandagupta.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalidasa** was a renowned Sanskrit poet and playwright, known for **works **such as **Shakuntala** and **Meghaduta.**
 
• **Vishakhadatta **was a playwright who wrote the famous **Sanskrit play Mudrarakshasa.**
 
• **Bhasa **was another famous Sanskrit playwright, known for **works **like **Svapnavasavadatta** and **Urubhanga.**

** Allahabad Pillar:**

 
• The **Allahabad Pillar** is a stambha that was **erected by Ashoka**, the Mauryan emperor who reigned in the** 3rd century BCE.**
 
• It is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It contains one of Ashoka's edicts.
 
• The** later inscriptions** attributed to the Gupta emperor **Samudragupta in the 4th Century CE **and the Mughal emperor **Jahangir in the 17th Century CE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Highways** are maintained by the **Central Public Works Department (CPWD).**
 
• **State Highways** are maintained by the **State Public Works Department (PWD).**
 
• **Border Roads** are maintained by the **Border Roads Organisation (BRO).**
 
• **District Roads** are maintained by the** Zila Parishad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CPWD** is responsible for the c**onstruction and maintenance of government buildings, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure projects**.

 
 
• It works **under** the **Ministry of Urban Development(MoUD).**
 
• It was **established in July 1854 **by** Lord Dalhousie** to execute public works. He also set up the Ajmer Provincial Division.
 
 
 
• **PWD **is responsible for the **construction and maintenance of state highways, major district roads, and other infrastructure projects in the states.**
 
• **BRO** is responsible for the** construction and maintenance of roads and bridges in border areas** of India.
 
 
• It is a statutory body **under** the ownership of the **Ministry of Defence(MoD).**
 
• It was** formed on 7 May 1960**
 
 
 
• The Zila Panchayat or **District Development Council or Zilla Parishad** or District Panchayat is the third tier of the Panchayati Raj system and functions at the district levels in all states.
 
 
• The members of the State Legislature and the members of the Parliament of India are members of the Zila Parishad. 
 
• The chairmen of all the Panchayat Samitis under the district are the ex officio members of Zila Parishad.
 
• It is headed by a president and a vice-president.
 
• **District Roads are maintained by the Zila Parishad.**

questions.question: In the expenditure method, GDP ≡ Sum total of all the final _____ received by the firms in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**expenditures.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The expenditure method** is one of the three ways to **calculate the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country**, the other two being the **production method** and the **income method.**
 
• **In the expenditure method**, **GDP is calculated by adding up all the final expenditures** made on goods and services produced within the country's borders. These expenditures could be made by households, businesses, government, or foreigners.
 
• **Final expenditures** refer to the purchases made by the end-users of the goods and services, and not the intermediate purchases made by businesses to produce those goods and services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue** refers to the **total income earned **by firms in the economy.
 
• **Gross domestic product (GDP)** is the standard measure of the** value of final goods and services produced by a country for a particular time.**
 
• GDP = private consumption + gross investment + government investment + government spending + (exports-imports).
 
• The calculation of GDP can be done on a quarterly, monthly, half-yearly, or annual basis.
 
• There are **3 Methods of GDP Calculation**:

 
• **Income Approach**: we calculate the income earned by all the factors of production in an economy.
 
• **Expenditure Approach**: measures the total expenditure incurred by all entities on goods and services within the domestic boundaries of a country.
 
• **Output (Production) Approach**: measures the monetary or market value of all the goods and services produced within the borders of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following is a risk with regard to the Green Revolution?

options.text: Increased disparities between small and big farmers
Increase in productivity in food grains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased disparities between small and big farmers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Green Revolution,** which **refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds**, **fertilizers**, and **pesticides **in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers.
 
• **Due to the high cost of these inputs**, **small farmers often find it difficult to adopt the new technologies** and compete with larger, wealthier farmers who can afford them.
 
• As a result, it has **led to increased disparities between small and big farmers**, with the latter reaping most of the benefits. This has led to a concentration of land and wealth in the hands of a few, while many small farmers have been pushed into debt and poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Green Revolution:**

 
• The **Green Revolution **was a major initiative that aimed to increase the production and quality of food crops, especially wheat and rice, in India, by introducing new technologies, such as high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, irrigation, and mechanization.
 
• **MS Swaminathan** is considered the **father of the Green Revolution in India.**
 
• **Norman Borlaug** is known as the** 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world**.
 
• the **Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965** under the **Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).**
 
• The Green Revolution within India led to an increase in agricultural production, especially in Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the name of the Southernmost tip of India?

__
 
• **Indira Point** is located **on the Great Nicobar Island**, which is a part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It is the **southernmost tip of Indian territory.**
 
• It was **previously known as Pygmalion Point** before being renamed as Indira Point in honor of the former Indian Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi.
 
• The area around Indira Point is prone to earthquakes and tsunamis due to its location in the seismic zone.
 
• The **Indira Point lighthouse** was **commissioned **into service on **30 April 1972.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Col **is located on the **Indira Ridge of Siachen Muztagh in the Karakoram Range**.

 
 
• It is a **high-altitude pass** located** in the Himalayas**, near the India-China border.
 
 
 
• **Karakoram** is a** mountain range located** in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, **near **the** borders of India, Pakistan, and China.**
 
• **Point Calimere** is a cape located on the southeastern coast of India, in the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
 
• It is the **easternmost point of Tamil Nadu.**

questions.question: Criminal law amendment act 2018, increased minimum punishment for rape of women from 7 to _________ years.
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**10.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **The Criminal Law Amendment Act 2018** was enacted in response to the increasing cases of sexual violence against women in India. • It has** increased the minimum punishment for rape of women from 7 to 10 years**. • The act also** introduced the death penalty as a possible punishment for the rape of girls under the age of 12** and increased the minimum punishment for gang rape and rape of a minor to 20 years and life imprisonment, respectively.

questions.question: Under the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court can issue ________ for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Writs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Writs** are legal orders issued by the **Supreme Court under Article 32** and by **High Courts under Article 226.**
 
• It is used to **enforce** any of the **fundamental rights conferred by Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These writs are issued to ensure that the rights of citizens are protected and any violation of their rights is addressed promptly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are** five types of writs** that can be** issued by the Supreme Court**:

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus** is issued to ensure that a person who has been detained or arrested is produced before the court.
 
• **Mandamus** is issued to compel a public official to perform their duties.
 
• **Prohibition** is issued to prevent a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari** is issued to quash an order passed by a lower court.
 
• **Quo Warranto** is issued to enquire into the legality of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Ordinances** are similar to laws, except that they are **issued by the President of India** when the **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, or both are not in session.**
 
• **Article 123** deals with the **ordinance-making power of the President.**
 
• **Article 213** deals with the **ordinance-making power of the Governor.**

questions.question: Who has the power to recommend for the imposition of Constitutional Emergency in a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Governor of the state.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor of the state** has the power to **recommend** for the **imposition of Constitutional Emergency in a state.**
 
• A **Constitutional Emergency or President's Rule or State Emergency** can be **imposed by the President under Article 356** of the Indian Constitution when the Governor of a state believes that the state cannot be governed according to the Constitution.
 
• The Governor can recommend the imposition of a Constitutional Emergency to the President of India. If the President is satisfied that a Constitutional Emergency is necessary, he can issue a proclamation imposing the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352 to 360 in Part XVIII** of the Constitution of India deals with the **emergency provisions**.
 
• There are **three types of emergencies** specified by the Constitution.
 
 
• **National Emergency:** Under **Article 352**, the president can declare a **national emergency** when the security of India or a part of it is threatened **by war or external aggression or armed rebellion.**
 
• **President's Rule: Article 356** empowers the President to issue a proclamation if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution.
 
• **Financial Emergency: Article 360** empowers the president to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: The green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about ______ of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem are able to capture and convert approximately 1 percent of the total energy from sunlight into food energy through photosynthesis.
 
• This low percentage is due to a phenomenon called the 'limiting factor', which refers to the factor that limits the rate of photosynthesis.
 
• Photosynthesis is the biological process by which plants convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose (a form of sugar) and oxygen. 
 
• This process takes place in specialized structures within plant cells called chloroplasts, which contain a pigment called chlorophyll that gives plants their green color.
 
• During photosynthesis, chlorophyll absorbs the energy from sunlight.
 
• This energy is used to power a series of chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limiting factors** affect the **rate of a reaction**. A condition that, when insufficient, causes a reaction's rate to slow down is known as a limiting factor.

 
 
• **Temperature, carbon dioxide content, and light intensity** are the** three main constraints on photosynthesis**.

questions.question: The athletes while throwing the discus have to remain inside a circle of how many diameter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5 meters.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** ****Discus throw** is a t**rack and field event** in which the athlete throws a heavy discus as far as possible.
 
• The discus throw is one of the oldest Olympic events, dating back to ancient Greece.
 
• Essentially, an athlete throws the metal disc by standing inside a **2.5-meter-diameter circle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** discus **has a metallic rim and a circular edge and can be constructed from metal, plastic, fiberglass, or wood. For **men**, it should have a **diameter of 22 cm**, and for **women, 18 cm.**
 
• The **weight of the discus** is fixed at **2kg for the men** and **1kg for women.** 
 
• This **circle is known as the throwing circle or the circle of release.**

questions.question: Who among the following authors incorporated the song Vande Mataram into his novel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.**__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's national song, Vande Mataram**, was written by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.**
 
• It was initially released in his book **Anandamath** (1882).
 
• Vande Mataram is a pair of **Sanskrit verses** written in a very elaborate Bengali script.
 
• It was** designated** as** India's National Song** by the **Constituent Assembly of India in 1950**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay** (also **Chatterjee**) was an Indian novelist, poet, essayist and journalist. Bengali literature refers to him as **'Sahitya Samrat'**, or the** Emperor of Literature**.
 
• **Murugam Periyar** was a social reformer from Tamil Nadu who worked for the upliftment of the lower castes and the eradication of social evils like untouchability. He is known as the** 'Father of the Dravidian movement'.**
 
• **Lal Makhan Singh** was a **Kenyan labor union leader** of Punjabi descent who is recognized for having laid the groundwork for trade unionism in that country. He is also known as **'Gujaratana Pita' (Father of Gujarat)** in Gujarat and Maharaja Nairobi in Kenya

questions.question: Who among the following personalities is an exponent of Indian classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rani Karnaa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Rani Karnaa**, an exponent Indian classical dancer who gained recognition for her proficiency in the **kathak dance **technique, is regarded by many as one of the finest practitioners of the genre.

questions.question: This underemployment is hidden in contrast to someone who does not have a job and is clearly visible as unemployed. Hence, it is also called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised employment** refers to a situation where a **person is employed but is not fully utilized** or is **working in a job that is below their skill level.**
 
• It can occur in various forms, such as** part-time work, temporary work, or low-paying jobs**, which do not fully utilize a person's skills and abilities.
 
• This type of underemployment is often hidden or not easily noticeable, unlike unemployment, where a person is actively looking for a job but cannot find one.
 
• It can have adverse effects on an individual's income, career growth, and overall job satisfaction.
 
• Disguised employment is a prevalent issue in developing countries, where a significant proportion of the workforce is engaged in low-paying or informal jobs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word "**unemployment**" describes people who are **actively looking for work** and are **employable** **but are having difficulty finding it.**
 
• **Cyclic unemployment** refers to the unemployment that occurs **due to fluctuations in the business cycle**, where there is a decline in economic activity, leading to a decrease in demand for labor.
 
• **Frictional unemployment** refers to the **temporary unemployment** that occurs **due to the time and effort required** to match job seekers with **suitable job** openings.
 
• **Open employment **refers to a situation where there are **job vacancies available**, and **employers are actively seeking to hire workers**.

questions.question: Maximum number of electrons that can filled in a shell is given by _______ where n is orbit number.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2n2**____** **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **orbit number, or principal quantum number (n)**, represents the **energy level of an electron** in an atom. The higher the value of n, the higher the energy level of the electron.
 
• The formula for calculating the **maximum number of electrons in a shell is given by 2n****2**, where n is the orbit number.
 
• For example, the first shell (n = 1) can have a maximum of 2 electrons, the second shell (n = 2) can have a maximum of 8 electrons, and so on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The arrangement of an element's electrons in various shells and subshells is referred to as its electron configuration.
 
• **Bohr** put forward a model of the atom **in 1913** (known as **Bohr's Atomic model**) that showed how the electrons were arranged in successive orbits.
 
• **Danish physicist Niels Henrik David Bohr **was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.**
